scope: adding 15 zero bits CHANGED where the block stops (55 instead of 65), so the 'surplus' was the client reading our tail until it saw has-ps = 0
the_insight: with no padding the block consumed 65 bits = 49 of our field plus 16 bits of the hybrid tail that followed
with 15 zeros before the terminator it stopped at 55 = 49 + 6
so the block keeps LOOPING after the first field and terminates on the first has-ps bit it reads as 0 - which is whatever zero bit it encounters next
that means the 'fixed trailer' interpretation was wrong: there is no fixed trailer, there is an under-terminated loop reading our tail
the_remaining_six_bits: 55 - 49 = 6, so after the delta the block reads SIX bits before it consumes the has-ps that exits it

a plausible candidate is the hint2 radar entry from the cols encoder: one gate bit plus six payload bits - if this build reads the gate as 1 it would consume exactly six more, but our padding is zeros
so the 6 bits must come from something else and need a direct measurement
next: sweep the padding length (0, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8) and record the measured ps length for each
the measured length as a function of the padding pins the exact number of bits read after the delta, and therefore where the has-ps terminator must be written
